characters.name: Darrow au Andromedus
characters.description: A young miner who is devastated by the execution of his wife, Eo. He initially seeks to join her in death but struggles with the realization that he may have betrayed her final wish for him to 'live for more.'
key_events: Cut down and buried Eo's body

characters.name: Eo
characters.description: Darrow's wife who was executed for singing a forbidden song. Her death acts as the inciting incident for Darrow's journey and inspires a potential rebellion among the Reds.
key_events: Urged the crowd to 'Break the chains!'

characters.name: Uncle Narol
characters.description: Darrow's cynical but caring uncle who provides guidance and support, even if he views Darrow's actions as futile. He eventually aids Darrow's death at the scaffold.
key_events: Pulled on Darrow's feet to hasten his death

characters.name: Dio
characters.description: Eo's younger sister who is deeply traumatized by the execution. She is called to the scaffold by Eo to receive a final message.
key_events: Spoke to Eo before her death

characters.name: Leanna
characters.description: Darrow's sister who helps hide his injuries and assists in the quiet handling of Eo's remains.
key_events: Watched Darrow drag Eo's body to the ventilation duct

relationships.description: Deeply in love, their relationship is tragically severed by Eo's execution, leaving Darrow broken and searching for meaning.
moments: Darrow burying her under a tree

relationships.description: A complicated family bond defined by shared grief, cynicism, and an understanding of the harshness of their lives.
moments: Uncle Narol pulling Darrow's feet at the gallows

world_facts.description: A tradition of rhythmic thumping on chests in memory of the deceased.
The gravity on Mars is low enough that hanging victims do not always die instantly, requiring loved ones to pull the body to break the neck.
The rallying cry issued by Eo before her death, which appears to have been secretly broadcast to the community.

summary: Following the execution of his wife, Eo, Darrow is consumed by grief and a desire to join her in death. The chapter depicts the immediate aftermath, including the community's somber Fading Dirge and the oppressive presence of the Golds' surveillance. Darrow, feeling empty and aimless, manages to steal Eo's body from the gallows with the silent cooperation of the community's women, eventually burying her in the place where they once shared their dreams. During this period, he is joined by his Uncle Narol, who provides a grim form of comfort and acknowledges the inevitability of the tragedy. Darrow realizes that by choosing death, he is failing to honor Eo's final plea to 'live for more.' Despite this realization, he lacks the strength to continue, succumbing to his depression and a sense of futility. He eventually stands on the same scaffold where his wife died. In a final act of mercy, his Uncle Narol pulls his feet to ensure his passing is swift. As he dies, Darrow reflects on the pain of his choices, realizing too late that his suicide was not a victory for their cause but a surrender to the cruelty of his world.
